evidence.claim: SDK-reachable and CLI-reachable artifact key sets are equal in both directions on a live end-to-end SDK-driven council.

probes.raw_output: live subprocess CLI inspect keys equal SDK keys

evidence.claim: An end-to-end SDK-driven council builds a CouncilSpec, executes it, and inspects a typed CouncilResult (not a string).

probes.raw_output: CouncilResult and all artifact values are dataclasses/enums

falsifiable_answers.sdk_cli_key_parity: Equal on the live fixture. sdk_minus_cli=[] cli_minus_sdk=[] keys=['budgets', 'decision', 'events', 'integrity', 'meta', 'outcome', 'plan', 'spec', 'stopping', 'transcript', 'votes']. Hiding CLI key 'votes' makes sdk_minus_cli=['votes'] (parity FAILS).
falsifiable_answers.typed_not_string: execute returns CouncilResult; decision.status is DecisionStatus; assert_typed_result passed.

negative_controls.description: Hide artifact key 'votes' from the CLI inspect payload. Parity must FAIL (sdk - cli == ['votes']); the unhidden good state must remain equal.

question: Implement tools/council/sdk.py so a CouncilSpec can be built, executed and inspected programmatically from another workflow, returning typed results rather than text. Falsifiable question: is every artifact reachable through the SDK also reachable through the CLI, and vice versa - or do the two surfaces expose different truths?
